description: Lunch! On the weekly changing, plant-based menu there's always a sandwich, a soup, and a special at a lower price and better quality than just about anywhere in Amsterdam! Café Gilde has a homely, relaxing atmosphere at lunchtime, with music you wouldn't likely hear anywhere else, interesting and often unusual food and drink, art on display, and of course een gezellige gastheer. Come with your weirdo mates, your dog (on the lead), your laptop, your kids, your art project, your pet brick, anything. Feel free to sit all afternoon with your work, feel free to chat to anyone and no one, feel free to buy an espresso and dip straight back out. We've got board games, a PS4, books, magazines, a USB-C cable - the lot. Come if you're transgender, come if you're autistic, come if you're disabled, come if you're none of the above; all are welcome except fascists. I mean it.
title: Lunch at Café Gilde

description: We’re excited to welcome the 5th edition of CineCarib to Ventilator Cinema on Saturday, October 17 at 15:00 , presented together with Caribbean Creativity and Africadelic. This edition features a special screening of Kombiná , a feature documentary exploring contemporary (Dutch) Caribbean architecture through 25 years of design work by architect Lyongo Juliana . The programme also includes Forsa Ansestral , a short documentary about tambú, an Afro-Caribbean musical and cultural tradition rooted in resistance, spirituality and community. Following the screenings, the filmmakers will join us for a panel discussion exploring the past, present and future of preserving cultural heritage in the Dutch Caribbean and its diaspora . Join us at Ventilator Cinema for an afternoon of film, architecture, music, heritage and conversation. MAIN FILM — KOMBINÁ Director: Lyongo Juliana Year: 2024 Locations: Curaçao, Bonaire, Saba & the Netherlands Languages: Papiamentu, Dutch & English Subtitles: English Duration: 69 min SHORT FILM — FORSA ANSESTRAL Director: Gyoni Jamanika Year: 2026 Produced by: Sendebibu Duration: 20 min About Kombina What defines contemporary Caribbean architecture? We have asked ourselves this question many times while designing new projects on the Dutch Caribbean islands. After 25 years of work in the Caribbean, we wanted to document our work and visualize the search for an answer to this question.Everyone knows what you mean when you talk about Caribbean music. Styles such as reggae, calypso, soca, salsa, zouk and merengue are known worldwide. This music emerged from a mix of African, European and other influences, characteristic of Caribbean culture. But architecture in the Caribbean is often reduced to traditional styles: Curacao's colorful facades, Bonaire's historic slave houses, and Saba's gingerbread trims. While beautiful, these images only scratch the surface of the islands' architectural diversity and innovation. Especially when it comes to contemporary architecture, there has been very little documented until now. So, what does contemporary Caribbean architecture actually look like? And what influence do climate, migration and heritage, for example, have on it? For us, like the local music and language, architecture is a mix of influences. Our documentary Kombina, which literally translates as "mixed", tells the story of how our contemporary projects reflect the local culture. About Lyongo Juliana Lyongo Juliana is a Curacaoan-Dutch architect whose work bridges the Netherlands and the Caribbean. Born in Utrecht and raised in Curacao, he studied architecture at Pennsylvania State University before completing his education in Architecture and Urbanism at Eindhoven University of Technology. Over the past 25 years, Juliana has designed numerous projects in the Caribbean and the Netherlands, combining sensitivity to local culture and climate with a strong commitment to the social role of architecture. As founder of lyongo architecture, with offices in Amsterdam and Willemstad, Juliana advocates for more diverse and inclusive approaches to architecture and urban development. In 2020, he served as Architect in Residence at the Amsterdam Architecture Centre (Arcam), where he researched diversity and inclusivity in the built environment, and subsequently continued this work as a fellow in Pakhuis de Zwijger's Designing Cities for All programme. His architectural projects include the Curacao Medical Center and various residential, educational and urban developments across the Caribbean and the Netherlands. About Forsa Ansestral Forsa Ansestral follows one week in the lives of tambu artists and elders from Curacao, Aruba, Bonaire, and the Dutch Caribbean diaspora as they come together for performances, workshops, gatherings, and conversations. Through these intimate encounters, the documentary explores tambu, an Afro-Caribbean musical and cultural tradition rooted in resistance, spirituality, and community, as a living archive of ancestral knowledge. Moving between generations and across borders, the film examines how heritage is embodied, transmitted, and continually reshaped. Conversations about gender, spirituality, modernization, and tradition reveal both tensions and connections within the community, while rhythm, movement, storytelling, and performance become vehicles for collective memory and healing. Forsa Ansestral ultimately asks what it means to inherit a cultural tradition, what responsibilities come with carrying it forward, and who gets to define its essence and shape its future. About Gyoni Jamanika and Sendebibu Gyoni Jamanika is a Curacaoan cultural researcher and heritage practitioner whose work engages with Caribbean history, cultural memory, identity, and the transmission of knowledge across generations. Jamanika has been involved in research on Caribbean genealogy and historical archives and has contributed to initiatives concerned with making Caribbean histories and cultural heritage more accessible. Jamanika is connected to Sendebibu, a community-led collective dedicated to preserving, sharing, and activating the cultural heritage of Curacao and the wider Dutch Caribbean. Through dialogue, workshops, performances, and intergenerational encounters, the collective creates spaces in which heritage is not simply documented but experienced and carried forward. Its work places particular emphasis on decolonization, community service, and connecting generations. One of Sendebibu's recent projects is Forsa Ansestral, developed around tambu in collaboration with Museo di Tambu Shon Cola. About Caribbean Creativity Caribbean Creativity is a Kingston- and Amsterdam-based non-profit organization that is committed to the programming and promotion of Caribbean and Caribbean-themed cinema. Over the years, Caribbean Creativity has hosted over 350 screenings, including numerous premieres. In 2020, they launched YardVibes, a streaming platform featuring content from independent Caribbean and African filmmakers. YardVibes currently offers over 100 titles, including feature films, web series, documentaries, and short films, with new content added monthly. For more information, visit www.caribbeancreativity.nl About Africadelic Africadelic is an organization and platform committed to the programming and promotion of African and African diasporic cultural creativity, diversity and activism in the Netherlands. The annual Africadelic Festival is an ode to the African continent and its worldwide diaspora, and offers a showcase of the cultural wealth and profound influence Afrodescendants have on global culture and society. Taking place from May 20-27, 2026, this year's festival offered another week filled with concerts, films, and talks. At the same time, they are (co-)organizing one-off events throughout the year, including CineCarib in collaboration with Caribbean Creativity. For more information, visit www.africadelic.com Running Order 14:45 - Doors open 15:00 - Introduction by Angel Misier 15:08 - Short film: Forsa Ansestral (20 minutes; to follow shortly) 15:28 - Feature film: Kombiná (69 minutes) 16:37 - Q&A with the filmmakers, moderated by Angel Misier 17:10 - End of Q&A. Clear the auditorium; conversations can continue in the bar.
title: CineCarib NL (Ed. 5): Kombiná + Forsa Ansestral (Special Screening)

description: After several requests, 4bid offers a new series of life drawing weekend intensives! This four-lesson weekend course covers all you need to know (or need a nudge to remember to put into practice) when it comes to model drawing. Over the 4 sessions (Friday to Monday, each 3h) you'll delve much deeper into the subject matter than in our regular 1,5h weekly appointments. Under the tutor's guidance, you will cover composition, anatomy, and shading. In each lesson, you'll work with the same live model, to master the understanding of their shapes. You will be invited to immediately develop and own a personal style, focusing on chiaro-scuro and line work, and applying bold gesture onto the paper. On the last evening you'll further one drawing, finishing it by applying all the learned tools. To get the most out of this course, it can be helpful to have taken part to a drop-in session at 4bid gallery on either Tuesdays or Sundays (see the regular meetups). It is however not required to have prior experience. The suggested price is €180 pp | 4 lessons of 3 hours | 8 participants max | Includes materials, coffee, tea, and snacks. If you have difficulties meeting this cost please let us know via email, and we can arrange something you are comfortable with: email@example.invalid. Classes are on Friday from 18:00 to 21:00, Saturday and Sunday from 16:00 to 19:00 and Monday from 18:00 to 21:00. Location: 4bid gallery, Overtoom 301, 1054HW AMSTERDAM
title: Life Drawing Weekend Intensive

description: Dinner! Dindins! One of Café Gilde's cooks will be at the helm to bring something affordable, accessible, delectable, and sometimes, just a bit batty. The deal is €10 for a main and a drink, with desserts available. Easy peasy. No obstacle is too high for us, so if you plan to come and have any dietary needs, let us know in advance and you'll see what a cook who actually cares about their craft does. We relish the challenge, if you want to call it as much. Just as long as it's vegan.
title: Dinner at Café Gilde

description: A night that moves from eerie, groove-driven post-punk to nostalgic indie rock and ends with deep, percussive disco. Combo Qazam Combo Qazam is a post-punk band from Utrecht that relies heavily on grooves and eerie vocal harmonies. On their well-received debut Flight Music (2020), they link this to 90s indie, math rock, prog and krautrock. Rhythmic and mechanical, yet nostalgic like a warm glow. On their second album Ghost Interior (2022), the band pursues the suffering of being human. For fans of Wire, Battles, Beak>, Tortoise, Pinback, Unwound, Can and Devo. Insta // Spotify // Bandcamp Viva Rosa Inspired by the great noise bands of the late eighties and early nineties, Viva Rosa plays indie rock with a hint of alt-country and Americana. With the passing of frontman and founder Mathieu Rosmuller, the band came to an abrupt end in 2009. Since then they've reunited a handful of times to perform his beautiful songs. Now in a new line-up, consisting of the remaining members of Viva Rosa together with two close friends, they are working on new material. Insta // Spotify Sentinel Island Disco Besides being a record label and club night, Sentinel Island Disco is a DJ duo that has its roots in Amsterdam. Moreover, it is a fictional island where the inhabitants seem to have eccentric party rituals. If you want to know what that looks like, you'll have to dock at Sentinel Island. Someone like Barbara Boeing or San Soda likes to go there too. Think obscure soca, ecstatic (afro) disco and deep percussive grooves from Sentinel's dark jungles. Insta // Spotify // Soundcloud
title: Viva Rosa + Combo Qazam
